segments.text: Earth is crooked. And a crash did it.
Our planet spins tipped over, leaning 23 and a half degrees.
Why? Long ago, baby Earth was hit by huge planet-sized rocks.
Scientists think one giant crash knocked it sideways… and it never stood back up.
That lean is why we have seasons.
When your half tips toward the Sun, sunlight hits straight on. Summer!
When it tips away, the light spreads thin. Winter.
Now the crazy part: in January, Earth is 5,000,000 kilometers closer to the Sun than in July.
Yet it's winter up north. Distance doesn't make seasons. The tilt does.
One crash, billions of years ago… is why you get summer.
